description: CTIF World Fire Statistics is the main international compilation of how many fires happen, how many people they kill and injure, and how fire services are resourced, country by country and for major cities. It is produced by the Center for Fire Statistics of CTIF, the international association of fire and rescue services, from responses to its requests to national fire services and from published official statistical reports. Report 31, published in 2026 with data for 2024, covers 40 countries with about 1.5 billion people and 26 cities, and earlier reports go back to data for 2005. Tables give fires, fire deaths and injuries and related fire service indicators as each country reports them, with rates per head of population and long-term overviews, in English, German and Russian editions. The reports are free and available to download as PDF files from the CTIF website. Caveats: every country has its own rules for counting fires, deaths and injuries, which change over time, coverage varies from year to year, and the tables are in PDF so they must be extracted. Simulation uses: setting baseline fire incident and casualty rates by country, and scaling fire service capacity in multi-country emergency response and risk models. Related records: the German fire service statistics (data-dfv-german-fire-service-statistics) and Statistics Canada fire statistics (data-statcan-incident-based-fire-statistics) are national sources that feed comparisons like this.
